hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions: the gate catches an unchecked action planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant P6 (plants/plants.diff) is in the kernel's PermissionAuthorizationHandler (src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Security/Permissions.cs). It passes any permission check when the route value id or userId equals the caller's own user id ('people may always manage their own record'). The plant is live. CriticR11Proof failed with it: a no-roles user with a Bearer token got 200 from GET /api/identity/users/{self}, GET /api/identity/users/{self}/access and GET /api/tenancy/access/{self}. The same test passed without the plant (plant-P6PROOF.log, plant-P6NONE.log). CriticR11Escalation showed a write: with the plant, the no-roles user's PUT /api/identity/users/{self} answered 200 and changed its displayName to 'Changed without permission' and its language to ar (plant-P6ESC.log). NOT CAUGHT. G2 plus the Rules gates ran 86 tests and exited 0 (plant-P6.log). G1 plus SelfTests ran 101 tests (plant-P6G1.log). Their only failures were static scans of the other plants' inert text, plus two GateSelfTests 'unexpected oracle' failures caused by roleIds order, which is not P6. The Kernel and module test projects ran 452 tests and all exited 0 (plant-P6M.log). Cause: G2PermissionTests.Request (tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G2/G2PermissionTests.cs:1035-1043) fills every route id with Guid.NewGuid() and every body with {}, so no deny or grant-one matrix ever names the caller's own id.

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the gate catches leaks planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant L6 keeps list totals for 120 s in an instance field of the singleton kernel ListBinding, keyed by search and filter with no tenant. It was caught three ways: by G1ProcessStateTests ('reachable Erp.Kernel.Lists.ListBinding`1._warmTotals ... from singleton ModuleCatalog'), by G1NonInterferenceTests ('92 answers depend on the other tenant's activity') and by G1HttpIsolationTests ('GET /api/identity/users?search=bravocnry... total 1 but for a value that exists nowhere total 0') (plant-L6.log, 25 min). Plant L7 removes the transaction-marker check from the kernel SQL erp.current_tenant_id(). It was caught live by G1DatabaseIsolationTests.A_tenant_set_for_the_whole_connection_or_left_by_an_earlier_transaction_is_ignored (expected 0 rows, saw 30) and statically by G1TenantSettingCodeTests (plant-L7DB.log).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: critic's live attack (API, documented query parameters, switch inputs, exports, files, side channels, DB roles)
hard_gates.evidence: attack/attack.mjs (the r10 critic's script, logic unchanged) ran as the alnoor admin (A) against gulfsteel (B), with B's canary user, saved views, logo, roles and users in place. Coverage: 109 operations, 686 documented query-parameter requests, 465 switch-input requests, 100 exports and 35 filters. Result: LEAKS 0. No id appeared in both tenants' answers, and A's totals did not move when B wrote. B's per-table md5 checksums were identical before and after (attack/attack-run.log). The first run reported a checksum change. Its only difference was where psql's 'DO' line fell between stdout and stderr (every NOTICE line was identical; attack/run1, attack/checksum-note.txt), so the checksum now compares NOTICE lines only. All 17 tenant tables have tenant_id NOT NULL with RLS enabled and forced, owned by erp_owner. erp_app with no tenant bound sees 0 users, audit rows and companies. erp_app is refused on sign_in_secret, sign_in_failures, the migration history, ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE RLS, pg_class, pg_stat_user_tables and pg_stats. A session-level tenant setting binds nothing.

biggest_gap.title: The permission gate (G2) never calls an endpoint with the caller's own id, so a kernel fault that lets anyone act on their own record passes every test
biggest_gap.detail: Every G2 matrix (A_user_whose_roles_grant_nothing_is_denied_everything, Granting_exactly_one_permission_opens_exactly_the_endpoints_that_declare_it and the carrier matrices) builds its requests with G2PermissionTests.Request. That method fills each route value with Guid.NewGuid() and each body with {}. So a permission decision that depends on route values is never tested: the caller's own user id, a record the caller created, or the caller's own company. Plant P6 in the kernel PermissionAuthorizationHandler passes any request whose id or userId is the caller's own. This is a common real-world shortcut ('people may always manage their own profile'). With it, a user with no roles read their own user record, access and sign-in history, and PUT their own user record (200: display name and language changed). Every gate and module test still passed, about 640 tests across G2, Rules, G1, SelfTests, Kernel and modules. For a UAE trading company, self-service screens are next: My payslip, my expense claims, my leave, my approvals. Each is an action on 'my own' record, and this gate would wave through a missing permission check on all of them. Fix: in G2, add the caller's own ids (user id, own session, a record the caller created, the caller's company and branch) to the route values each deny and grant-one matrix tries, next to the random id. Ratchet the count of self-referencing requests.
biggest_gap.evidence: Reproduce: apply plants/plants.diff (P6 hunk in src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Security/Permissions.cs) and add plants/CriticR11Proof.cs and plants/CriticR11Escalation.cs under tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/Critic/. Then run plants/run-in-toolbox.sh with PLANTS='P6PROOF P6NONE P6' (and run-in-toolbox-2.sh with 'P6ESC P6G1 P6M'). Results: CriticR11Proof fails only with CRITIC_PLANT=P6 (GET /api/identity/users/{self} -> 200 for noaccess@alpha.example). CriticR11Escalation shows 'PUT /api/identity/users/{self} displayName -> 200 ... "displayName":"Changed without permission","language":"ar"'. G2+Rules: 86 tests, exit 0 (plant-P6.log). Kernel and modules: 452 tests, exit 0 (plant-P6M.log). The cause is at tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G2/G2PermissionTests.cs:1037: endpoint.Path(_ => Guid.NewGuid().ToString()).

other_findings: The kernel Money type's invariants can be bypassed. This is the most important finding after the gate miss. Round 10's rounding gap is fixed: three lines of USD 1.00 at 3.6725 now total AED 11.02 (money-probe/output.txt). But Money is a public readonly record struct with public init setters, so these all compile and run without validation: `new Money { Amount = 100, Currency = "USD", ExchangeRate = 0, BaseAmount = 999 }`, `line with { BaseAmount = 50 }`, and JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Money> with the platform's own JSON options. The JSON read accepted currency 'usd', rate -2 and base 1 for amount 10.123456, and Add on the result returned -40.49 without complaint. Once p08 and the ledger accept Money in request bodies, an amount's stored base amount and rate can disagree with each other (CLAUDE.md rule 2). Fix: make the setters private, add a JsonConverter that goes through Create or Unrounded, and add a test (money-probe/Program.cs reproduces).

[route: p03-identity] The users list answers a user's roleIds in no fixed order. RolesOf in src/Modules/Identity/Erp.Modules.Identity/Users/UserEndpoints.cs:678 has no ORDER BY. Two identical requests listed the same two role ids in opposite orders, and the G1 differential oracle reported this as 'unexpected oracle'. That failed GateSelfTests.The_HTTP_attack_catches_planted_header_route_and_body_leaks in the critic's P6 gate run (plant-P6G1.log: the first difference is only the roleIds order). This can turn a verify red at random. Sort roleIds, or have the gate's normaliser treat id arrays as sets.
